title: EquiMem: Calibrating Shared Memory in Multi-Agent Debate via Game-Theoretic Equilibrium
abstract: arXiv:2605.09278v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Multi-agent debate (MAD) systems increasingly rely on shared memory to support long-horizon reasoning, but this convenience opens a critical vulnerability: a single corrupted entry can contaminate the downstream memory-augmented reasoning, and debate alone fails to filter such errors. Existing safeguards filter entries via heuristics or LLM-based validation, yet they rely on AI judgments that share the same failure modes and overlook the cross-agent dynamics of MAD. We address this gap by formulating memory updating in MAD as a zero-trust memory game, in which no agent is assumed reliable and the game's equilibrium motivates a principled objective for calibrating memory influence. translated_title: EquiMem：基于博弈论均衡的多智能体辩论共享记忆校准机制
translated_abstract: 多智能体辩论（MAD）系统日益依赖共享记忆来支持长程推理，但这种便利也带来了一个关键漏洞：单条被污染的记忆条目就可能污染下游的记忆增强推理，而仅靠辩论本身无法过滤此类错误。现有的防护机制通过启发式规则或基于大语言模型（LLM）的验证来过滤记忆条目，但它们所依赖的AI判断与被验证对象具有相同的失效模式，并且忽视了多智能体辩论中的跨智能体动态。为弥补这一空白，我们将多智能体辩论中的记忆更新形式化为一个“零信任记忆博弈”，其中不假设任何智能体是可靠的，而博弈的均衡为校准记忆影响力提供了一个原则性目标。在该目标的指导下，我们提出了 EquiMem——一种推理时校准机制，它将每条记忆更新与共享记忆状态以及其他智能体已在使用的记忆进行对照评估，并利用它们现有的检索查询和遍历路径作为（原文此处截断）……
tldr: 该论文提出 EquiMem，一种基于零信任记忆博弈均衡的推理时校准机制，通过将每条记忆更新与共享记忆状态及其他智能体已使用的记忆进行对照评估，防止多智能体辩论系统中单条错误记忆污染下游的推理过程。
en_tdlr: EquiMem is an inference-time calibration mechanism grounded in the equilibrium of a zero-trust memory game, which evaluates each memory update against the shared memory state and the memory already in use by other agents, thereby preventing a single corrupted entry from contaminating downstream memory-augmented reasoning in multi-agent debate systems.
